source.version: NBER Working Paper 33641, April 2025, The Cybernetic Teammate: A Field Experiment on Generative AI Reshaping Teamwork and Expertise (PDF pp. 1-2). The saved working paper is not the later Organization Science article identified in the citation record.
source.supplement_used: Appendix A (problem statements), Appendix B (evaluation), Appendix C (prompts), and Figure A1, PDF pp. 47-54, in the same PDF.

studies.label: P&G product-development field experiment: individual or team work, with or without AI
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Individual randomization within business-unit/geography strata, followed by random pairing in team conditions (PDF pp. 9-10). OLS uses one observation per solution and heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors, with no reported clustering (PDF p. 12). Teams are production units, not intact clusters randomized to treatment.

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3.2; PDF p. 41, Table 1, Individuals and Team participants rows (columns: no AI, AI)
counts_source.quote:
Our analyses focus on 776 of these participants who were randomly assigned across four conditions.
Individuals 154 155
Team participants 230 (115 Teams) 252 (126 Teams)

arms.name: Individual No AI (Control)
arms.description: Works alone without AI on the initial task; analysis-arm count is printed in Table 1 (PDF p. 41). Initial randomized allocation count is not reported.

arms.name: Team No AI (T1)
arms.description: Commercial and R&D professionals randomly paired to work through Microsoft Teams without AI; Table 1 prints 115 Teams (PDF p. 41).

arms.name: Individual + AI (T2)
arms.description: Works alone with the GPT-4-based tool after prompt training and provision of recommended prompts (PDF p. 10).

arms.name: Team + AI (T3)
arms.description: Randomly paired Commercial and R&D professionals work together with the same AI tool and training; Table 1 prints 126 Teams (PDF p. 41).

studies.country: Countries not stated; Europe and Americas (PDF p. 9).
studies.task: Develop and submit a solution to an innovation problem in the participant’s own business unit, addressing products, packaging, communication, or retail execution (PDF p. 10; Appendix A, PDF p. 47).

ai_tool.name: GenAI tool built on GPT-4 and accessed through Microsoft Azure; July-workshop participants had GPT-4o
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 3.2 and footnote 10; PDF p. 8 dates workshops to May-July 2024. Model release years are not stated.

preregistration.where: AEA RCT Registry, AEARCTR-0013603; https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/13603 (PDF p. 2; PDF p. 8, footnote 3). The analysis plan is described as embargoed.

estimates.notes: All model columns analyze the same full sample of solutions; alternative specifications are not independent samples. n_units is the printed all-arm regression observation count, not a people count or two-arm subtotal. Arm counts from Table 1 conflict with the prose total; no two-arm people total is printed. Treatment means are not calculated from intercepts and coefficients. Both contrasted arms submit one solution per person; uncertainty for this contrast is coded participant. Quality is standardized by the Individual No AI group before regression (PDF p. 13); the unprinted SD is not set to one. Quality is paper-primary, but its preregistered primary status is not established by the saved document. Primary-selection rationale: paper-primary outcome, free-use individual AI contrast, and the unadjusted specification discussed in the main results (PDF p. 14).

open_items: The prose states that analyses focus on 776 randomly assigned participants, and this printed count is retained as study n_analyzed (PDF p. 9). Table 1 prints different arm-level counts that are inconsistent with that total. The screening form supplies a computed total, which is not transcribed because it is not printed in this PDF. The exact participants underlying the regressions cannot be reconciled from the saved version.

The initial number assigned to each arm and initial randomization total are not separately reported. Participants from incomplete teams were reassigned to individual conditions (PDF p. 10, footnote 8); the number reassigned and whether AI status was retained are not reported.

The citation record identifies a later journal version, but the supplied PDF is the NBER working paper. Numerical results here are confined to the saved PDF; the later version may settle the count discrepancy and omitted outcomes.

No participant-level or output-level arm SDs are printed for the extracted outcomes. Quality is already standardized relative to the individual no-AI group; raw quality arm means and SDs are not printed (PDF p. 13). The appendix reports variance components for ratings, not the needed participant-level SDs (PDF p. 49).

For pairwise tests between nonbaseline arms, tables print p-values without coefficients, test statistics, degrees of freedom, or SEs of the differences. The baseline coefficients are not subtracted. Narrative-only comparisons remain records with null statistics.

Figure 13 has no printed arm levels, uncertainty, or analysis counts. Its note describes both distance from the condition mean and cosine distance between solutions; the embedding model and precise construction are not stated. No graphical values are digitized.
Novelty, feasibility, impact, business potential, and AI-rated robustness results have no printed arm contrasts in the supplied document.
The registry and preregistration are named, but the preregistered primary outcome is not identified in the saved document. Quality is explicitly primary in the paper (PDF p. 12).
The model names are given, but model release years are not printed; ai_tool.year is null. The workshop calendar year is not substituted for a release year.

Technicality bimodality coefficients are preserved in notes because the fixed stats schema has no arm-level distribution-shape fields. They must not be interpreted as arm means or standardized treatment effects.

Team contrasts use solution-level robust uncertainty after individual assignment and random pairing. The record conservatively codes their se_basis as output; the document reports no participant-clustered estimator.
The codebook has no dedicated word-count or AI-content-retention measure code. automated_score is used with explicit descriptions; neither is an automated creativity judgment.
notes: Read the complete markdown conversion from beginning to end, including references and all appendices, and checked every cited PDF page with pymupdf. PDF page numbers match printed page numbers where printed. Every numerical estimate is transcribed from the saved PDF; no means, SDs, two-arm totals, differences, test statistics, or intervals are derived. Printed precision is retained in the verbatim source quotes. All regression specifications are retained as alternative records on the same sample. Narrative-only and figure-only eligible contrasts are retained with null statistics; outcomes without any identified contrast and ineligible results are listed in not_extracted. Team-plus-AI versus individual-no-AI coefficients and the printed AI-design tests are included even where the screening map did not list them separately. Only initial-task between-person results are extracted; no after-AI outcome is reported. Study n_analyzed is the printed prose count, with conflicting printed arm counts preserved and explicitly flagged. The screening form lists no shared-sample paper.
